label: Microtopping · smooth fine cement (mid warm-grey, troweled, no chips)

source.selection_reason: топинг .jpg is a clean TOP-DOWN (face-on) shot of smooth grey microtopping with the characteristic subtle cloudy troweled mottling and NO chips — the truest microtopping in the folder. A purple towel + cosmetic jar occupy the LEFT ~40% behind a hard diagonal edge; the crop was taken from the clean right portion well clear of the object.
source.crop_reason: 2400px square in the centre-right clean microtopping zone, fully clear of the towel/jar diagonal edge (which only reaches the top-left and bottom-left corners of the image). Smooth, face-on, no scratches, no chips.
source.rejected_set: gray-old-scratched = strong diagonal scratch line + lighting gradient (reads 'old scratched'). background-natural-cement-brown = polished marble with a diagonal vein (reads marble, not microtopping). DSC08676 = heavily blurred (shallow DoF). DSC08740/08742 = oblique steps/floor with perspective + control-joint lines. Food/object photos (boiled-dough, anise-seeds, vegetables) excluded per brief.

material_truth.fillers: None — microtopping is a smooth fine cementitious/polymer skim coat (microcement). No aggregate/chips. Only subtle troweled cloud mottling and very fine grain.
material_truth.finish: Troweled smooth, matte-to-satin sealed. Near-flat surface relief.
material_truth.manufacturer_recipe: Microcement / microtopping system (e.g. Sika Sika-Microtopping or Topciment Microbase+Microdeck) — 1-3 mm fine cementitious skim over primer, finished with a matte/satin PU sealer.

colour.note: Very uniform surface after de-light (stdev ~7) — matrix hex ≈ overall mean. Mid warm-grey, neutral with a faint warm cast.

scale.physical_mm_per_tile: ~550-650 mm represented by the 2048px master (the cosmetic jar in the source gives scale ≈ 70 mm; the 2400px crop spans roughly 0.6 m of floor).
scale.tile_note: Microtopping is a broad seamless skim — a LOW tile count looks most authentic (large continuous field). 1-2 is ideal; 1.5 recommended. Higher tiling makes the subtle cloud mottling read as an obvious repeat. If the manifest 'tile' must be an integer, use 2.

gloss.note: Matte sealed microcement. roughness.png mean 0.721 (chipsSmooth=false → near-uniform high roughness with tiny luma modulation). 0.68-0.75 reads as matte; lower toward 0.5 for a satin-sealed look.

normal.png.strength: gen-pbr bump 3.0 (gentle — fine grain only); R range 102-153 i.e. ~+-26 of 128, low relief, correct for smooth microtopping

processing.decode: sharp JPG -> extract 2400px square (clean right zone) -> lanczos3 DOWNSCALE to 2048 (sharp, no upscaling).
processing.delight: sharp divide-by-heavy-blur (sigma scaled to ~72px, aggressive) re-multiplied by per-channel means. A stronger flatten was used deliberately to suppress the low-frequency troweled clouds so the field reads as even microtopping (its true character) and the tile-repeat of the cloud pattern is minimised.
processing.seamless: Half-offset (quadrant-swap) wrap + feathered cross-fade heal blending with a 180°-rotated copy of the offset (blur-heal was rejected — it leaves visible soft blotches on this flat low-frequency field). Validated by 2x2 tiling.
processing.pbr: scripts/gen-pbr-maps.js microtopping --root=3d-assets/textures-v4 (bump 3.0, baseRough 0.75, chipsSmooth false, ao 0.6).

caveats: Not upscaled — downscaled from a 2400px crop.
Object cropped out: a purple towel + cosmetic jar with a daisy occupied the left ~40% of the source; the crop excludes them entirely.

Microtopping is inherently a low-frequency cloudy field, so the 2x2 tile shows a faint soft repeat of the cloud mottling (no hard seam). The aggressive de-light reduces this; keep the manifest tile low (1.5-2) to keep it subtle.
Heavier de-light slightly idealises the colour toward an even mid-grey rather than a 1:1 match of the original lit clouds.

recommended_manifest.palette_note: matrix mid warm-grey, lighter cloud, darker cloud, deep shade variant
recommended_manifest.note: Repoint pbr.* to textures-v4/microtopping/* to use this new set. If manifest 'tile' is integer-only, use 2. (Orchestrator applies — do not edit manifest here.)
